newsitem.title: UK: Natpower, Powergen off on study report.
newsitem.headline: Natpower, Powergen off on study report.

text.p: Shares in National Power Plc and PowerGen Plc dropped in pre-market trade on Tuesday as a press report highlighted a study criticising the workings of the power generation market.
National Power shares were down 8p at 519-1/2 by 0724 GMT while PowerGen was down 5-1/2p at 673-1/2.

A Financial Times report said a review of the electricity market by a consultancy called London Economics, compiled for East Midlands Electricity, argued that the generators had an interest in preventing competition in retail electricity supply.
The consultancy said consumers would fail to benefit unless the two big generators were forced to sell more generating capacity, the FT said.

It also argued that the generators should be stopped from making long-term contracts with electricity distributors since such deals could inhibit competition in generation, locking consumers into high prices.

Taking up the theme, the FT's Lex column said proper competition was lacking in the power generation market and it may be difficult to tackle the problem without attacking the generators' remaining market position.
No-one at electricity regulator Offer was immediately available for comment. Officials at National Power and PowerGen were not immediately available either.
